claims.text: The initial material is standard Ti-6Al-4V with an untreated, annealed surface.
Plasma nitriding can increase the surface hardness of Ti-6Al-4V.
Plasma nitriding can increase the wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V.
Controlled nitrogen-plasma treatment promotes nitrogen diffusion into the titanium alloy.
Controlled nitrogen-plasma treatment forms a TiN-rich surface layer.
The treatment produces a surface-confined TiN or nitrogen-enriched layer with a compositional gradient into the substrate.
At elevated temperature, nitrogen introduced by plasma nitriding reacts with titanium to form TiN precipitates.
TiN precipitates significantly increase surface hardness.
The nitride layer acts as a wear-resistant barrier against sliding and abrasive forces.
Plasma-nitrided Ti-6Al-4V is expected to have at least 50% greater surface hardness than untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Plasma-nitrided Ti-6Al-4V is expected to have a lower wear rate than untreated Ti-6Al-4V under the same test conditions.
The expected benefit should hold in room-temperature pin-on-disk testing under moderate loads.
Moderate loads in the proposed pin-on-disk test simulate typical service stresses.
The enhancement is limited to an optimized plasma-nitriding parameter window.
At excessively low treatment temperatures, the nitride layer may be insufficiently formed.
At excessively high treatment temperatures, the nitride layer may degrade and limit the beneficial effect.
The hypothesis is falsified if treated samples show less than a 50% hardness increase or fail to show a consistent wear-rate reduction relative to untreated controls.
